thesis: Northrim BanCorp (Nasdaq: NRIM) is an Alaska bank holding company with community banking, home mortgage and specialty finance segments. Q3 2026 10-Q (statements, segment, nonaccrual and merger notes, MD&A highlights read) filed 2026-10-30. Q3 net income 14.4M ($0.63 diluted) versus 27.1M ($1.20); the prior-year quarter included a 13.9M gain on sale of assets by Pacific Wealth Advisors. Nine-month net income 43.4M ($1.92 vs $2.32). Q3 NIM 4.96% (+13bp). Total assets 3.58B (+8.8% in nine months), deposits 3.05B, equity 356.1M, tangible equity 305.3M. Nonaccrual loans net of guarantees rose to 40.1M from 12.0M at year end (C&I 27.4M vs 4.3M); Q3 provision 7.7M (Specialty Finance 8.4M provision, segment loss 4.3M) versus 1.7M. Pending all-stock acquisition of PBCO Financial (1.160 shares per share, PBCO holders to own about 21%, approved 2026-10-20, expected close about 2027-01-01). Close 24.05 on 2026-11-11: market cap about 535M, about 9.6x TTM net income (55.9M), 9.4x annualized nine-month EPS, 1.50x book and 1.75x tangible book, dividend 0.17 quarterly (2.8% yield). Cheap on earnings with high NIM, but credit quality deteriorated in the specialty finance and C&I books.
counterthesis: Nonaccrual loans tripled in nine months to 40.1M (about 1.7% of 2.40B loans; I did not read the loan total precisely beyond the maturity table) and Specialty Finance swung to a loss, so the low P/E may capitalize earnings that fall as provisions rise. The nine-month ACL of 33.3M covers 83% of nonaccrual, and part of it sits on loans with no ACL needed because of collateral or guarantees. The merger adds about 21% new shares and integration risk, and regulatory approval is still pending. TTM earnings include one-time gains that I did not isolate in Q4 2025. The bank is Alaska concentrated (economy tied to energy and government). Peers and ROTCE not compared; no CRE breakdown or capital ratios read.
invalidation: Nonaccrual above about 3% of loans, further Specialty Finance losses, provision above 10M a quarter, NIM below 4.5%, merger terms or approval failing, or CET1 falling below peer norms after the merger.
